title: Derived module evaluation is abelian cohomology on the slice
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of associative unital rings, without a commutativity assumption, and $M$ a sheaf of left $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Work in a common universe containing objects, arrows, coefficients and covering index sets; assume $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ has enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. For an object $W$ give $\mathcal C/W$ the localized topology, and let $M_{ab}|_W$ be the sectionwise restriction of the underlying abelian sheaf [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},W}:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be evaluation $N\mapsto N(W)$, and compute its right derived functors by injective module resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every integer $q\geq0$ there is a canonical additive isomorphism
$$ R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},W}(M)\cong H^q(\mathcal C/W,M_{ab}|_W), $$
where the right side is right derived evaluation at the terminal object $\operatorname{id}_W$ in abelian sheaves on the slice. The isomorphism is natural in $M$ and in degree zero identifies the two evaluations $M(W)$. No injectivity of $M_{ab}$ or flatness of $\mathcal O$ over the constant integer sheaf is assumed.

proof.text: Put A = SheafOfModules.toSheaf R, B = J.overPullback AddCommGrpCat W, T = A followed by B, and F = evaluation of abelian sheaves on the slice at id_W. A is exact: finite limits are preserved by the module forgetful functor, and finite colimits by the proved source instance SheafOfModules.preservesFiniteColimits_toSheaf. B is additive sectionwise, preserves finite limits as a continuous sheaf pushforward, and preserves colimits by Mathlib sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous for Over.forget W. Hence T is exact. T followed by F is definitionally module evaluation at W. The two abelian sheaf categories have enough injectives by their Grothendieck abelian instances.

source.place: Tags 03FD and 03F3; exact forgetting and sectionwise restriction

proof.text: For every injective module I and n > 0, apply lem-sc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic-zariski in its already proved arbitrary-site form to get H^n(W,A(I)) = 0. Transport zero across lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization to H^n(id_W,T(I)), and then across lem-sc-site-cohomology-right-derived-sections to R^n F(T(I)). Thus T sends injectives to F-acyclic objects. This uses neither injectivity of A(I) nor flatness over the integer sheaf.

source.place: Tag 03FD, positive cohomology of forgotten injective modules; Tag 03F3(2), slice localization

proof.text: For each module M choose its existing injectiveResolution I. Exactness of T makes T.mapResolution I.ι a resolution by F-acyclic objects. Compose I.isoRightDerivedObj (T followed by F) q with the inverse of F.rightDerivedObjIsoOfResolution on this mapped resolution. For a module morphism use InjectiveResolution.desc and its augmentation equation. Apply lem-sc-acyclic-comparison-natural and the naturality of isoRightDerivedObj; reassociation gives naturality of these components, defining e_q by NatIso.ofComponents. This is the existing public exact_comp_comparison construction already used in ModuleAbelianEvaluationComparison, now applied directly to T.

source.place: Tag 015E, acyclic resolutions and naturality of the comparison

proof.text: Apply lem-sc-ext-derived-composite to T and F. Its formula for all augmentation-compatible lifts identifies the constructed comparison with the canonical object comparison: compare on the chosen resolutions and canonical descOfQuasiIso lift, where both formulas reduce to the same homology map. The complex-composition isomorphism for the identity composite is the identity componentwise. Cancel the target resolution isomorphism to obtain exactly the displayed formula for arbitrary I, K and φ (the imported exact_comp_comparison_formula).

source.place: Tag 015M, exact-composite comparison and its formula via acyclic resolutions

proof.text: In degree zero take the chosen resolutions and canonical comparison lift. The augmentation compatibility equation implies equality after the inclusion of cycles, so cancel that inclusion to identify the two maps into cycles. Use toRightDerivedZero_eq, naturality of the homology projection, and the lift formula from the preceding step to show the two augmentations agree after the comparison. Cancel the target resolution isomorphism and conclude the displayed natural-transformation equation (the imported exact_comp_comparison_zero). Assemble the isomorphisms, this normalization, and the all-lifts formula. All arguments remain valid for the zero ring or module, noncommutative coefficients, and sites without a final object.

source.place: Tags 03FD and 03F3, comparison in degree zero and identity of section augmentations

Import and use the existing exact_comp_comparison, exact_comp_comparison_formula and exact_comp_comparison_zero from ModuleAbelianEvaluationComparison, made public in place in this repair. No duplicate helpers, new mathematical statements or new holes. The Precoverage-specialized theorem is not used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q26-674da8244 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 4 steps in full. The statement is unchanged and correct against Stacks Tag 03FD (sites-cohomology.tex lines 1862-1921) and Tag 03F3 (lines 608-642). No new nodes, no cycle, no SGA. Live and side-live still show the item unsplit with no repair note, so the delivery is not superseded. Step 1: the cited lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison states exactly the canonical, natural, degree-0-normalized isomorphism used; its ring is an arbitrary sheaf of rings (Lean uses RingCat) acting on the left, and its hypotheses match the item verbatim. Step 2: restricting an abelian injective resolution is elementary from two cited statements, exactness of restriction (lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-injectives) and preservation of injectives (lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization); the step does not assume module injectives are abelian injectives. Step 3: id_W is terminal, def-pur-localized-ringed-site gives sectionwise restriction, and def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology(2) gives the resolution-independence maps and H^0 = evaluation, so the complexes are identical and the step is elementary. It re-derives the localization isomorphism only to get the degree-0 identity, which the localization node does not state. Step 4 composes and pastes the naturality squares. Edge cases checked: point site with O = M = F_p (M injective as a module but not in Ab), O = M_2(F_p), M = 0, a site with no final object, and smallness of the slice. The duplicate search found only overlaps: the abelian-only localization node, lem-pe-injective-complex-slice-section-model (derived, constant ring) and det-pe-injective-acyclicity-reduction (commutative Λ). I accept the 3 declared tool_uses as generic site-cohomology facts that replace no step of the unit's route (main-20261015 sk-prop-sf-comparison proof, first paragraph).

reviewed_lean.note: Statement matches the node and Stacks 03FD/03F3(2) clause by clause. Left side: derived module evaluation at W in Mod(R).
